title: Calcium channel blockers: vessel or heart
ariaLabel: Schematic of L-type calcium channels in a blood vessel wall and in the heart. Depolarisation opens the channels, calcium enters, and vascular smooth muscle contracts while the heart speeds up, conducts and contracts harder. A dihydropyridine blocker mainly relaxes the vessel; verapamil and diltiazem act more on the heart.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or affinity is shown or implied.

blockInfo: A calcium channel blocker of the chosen class in the channel (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less calcium enters this tissue, so everything that depends on calcium entry is reduced.

nodes.label: Depolarisation
nodes.info: Depolarisation: the membrane potential rising towards threshold. Vascular smooth muscle and heart cells both open L-type calcium channels when this happens. The slider sets how strongly and how often.

nodes.label: Channel open
nodes.info: L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle opening with depolarisation.

nodes.label: Channel open
nodes.info: L-type calcium channels in the heart opening with depolarisation.

nodes.label: Vessel tone
nodes.info: Tone of the arterioles. Less calcium entry means a more relaxed vessel, lower resistance and lower blood pressure.

nodes.label: Heart rate and AV conduction
nodes.info: Sinus rate and conduction through the AV node. Verapamil and diltiazem slow both; this is why they are used for rate control in atrial fibrillation.

nodes.label: Contractility
nodes.info: Force of contraction. Calcium entry triggers calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, so less entry means weaker beats; this is why verapamil is avoided in heart failure with a low ejection fraction.

nodes.label: Calcium in the cell
nodes.info: Free calcium inside the vascular smooth muscle cell.

nodes.label: Calcium in the cell
nodes.info: Free calcium inside the heart cell.

edges.info: Depolarisation opening channels in vascular smooth muscle.
Depolarisation opening channels in the heart.

edges.label: L-type channel
edges.info: The L-type (high-voltage) calcium channel of vascular smooth muscle. Dihydropyridines bind it most readily here, because the resting membrane potential of vessels keeps many channels in the state the drug prefers.

edges.label: L-type channel
edges.info: The L-type calcium channel of the sinoatrial node, AV node and cardiac muscle. Verapamil and diltiazem bind a different site from dihydropyridines and block it most in fast-firing cells such as the nodes.
More calcium inside means more contraction of the vessel wall.
Calcium drives pacemaker and AV nodal activity.
Calcium drives contraction of cardiac muscle.

sources: Two groups of calcium channel blockers. Dihydropyridines act mainly on vascular smooth muscle and dilate arterioles; verapamil and diltiazem are also vasodilators but have clearly negative chronotropic, inotropic and dromotropic effects, slowing the rate, force and AV conduction. The two groups bind separate sites on the L-type channel (Review of calcium channel blockers, PMC; British and Irish Hypertension Society, calcium channel blockers).

Calcium and contraction. In smooth muscle calcium raises contraction through calmodulin and myosin light chain kinase; in the heart calcium entry triggers further release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum. This is standard physiology, in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and was not checked against a linked source here, so it is flagged for review.
simplified: Reflex tachycardia after a fast-acting dihydropyridine, ankle oedema, other calcium channel types (T-type, N-type), differences between individual drugs (and drugs within a group), use dependence and voltage dependence of block, interactions (digoxin, ciclosporin, beta-blockers), and the effect in heart failure or heart block are left out. Levels, flow and the size of the block are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
